configOptions.name: Autonomy
configOptions.description: on: the agent carries on after each turn while a step still waits for its gate, within the limit on tries per step. off: it stops at the end of each turn. Any message you type ends it.

prompt.text: Reply with exactly the one word: done

availableCommands.name: catalogue
availableCommands.description: Writes down what each class member and each package is for, so later questions about the code are answered from those descriptions instead of re-reading it. It changes no code, and a stopped run carries on where it left off.

availableCommands.name: chief-engineer
availableCommands.description: Reads the code a change touches, decides which engine tool performs it and with which arguments, and issues each as an instruction with exactly one possible execution for the worker. It never changes code itself.

availableCommands.name: debug
availableCommands.description: Diagnoses one reported bug: recalls what is already known about it, takes one measurement in the running program that tells the possible causes apart, and checks the fix. It replaces adding log lines to the code.

availableCommands.name: javadocs
availableCommands.description: Documents public Java API that has no documentation, using only what the compiler confirms about it. Where the meaning cannot be told from the code it leaves a marked gap for you rather than guessing.

availableCommands.name: main
availableCommands.description: Runs work that has several steps as a workflow: it declares the steps, drives them one at a time, and refuses to call a step done until that step's check has actually run.

availableCommands.name: observer
availableCommands.description: Watches a short window of an agent's recent tool calls beside the work, and says whether the agent is getting around a rule he gave. It never edits and is never waited on; a real finding refuses the next call with a correction addressed to the worker.

availableCommands.name: pm
availableCommands.description: Plans a piece of work and hands it to other seats with a brief, checks what comes back against the agreed checks, and records the result. It never writes code itself.

availableCommands.name: profile
availableCommands.description: Measures a running Java program and names, method by method, where the time goes. It replaces timers added to the code.

availableCommands.name: report
availableCommands.description: Turns failures jawata has recorded on this machine into a bug report you post from your own GitHub account. It only drafts: you read it and decide whether it is posted.

availableCommands.name: rottenmeier
availableCommands.description: Reads what made him angry or interrupt in the discussion, names what the agent did wrong, and proposes a rule that would have prevented it. He accepts or rejects each one; an accepted rule is injected into the agents it binds.

availableCommands.name: spec-auditor
availableCommands.description: Checks a sprint spec against the raw working notes and refuses it when a requirement was dropped, narrowed or softened. It loops with the spec editor until it signs off, before you see the spec.

availableCommands.name: spec-editor
availableCommands.description: Writes the clean sprint spec from the raw working notes, in plain language, for you to sign off. The spec auditor checks it against the notes first.

availableCommands.name: test-manager
availableCommands.description: Decides which tests a change actually needs and runs only those, instead of the whole suite. It runs the tests; whether the result passes is the project manager's decision.

availableCommands.name: cover
availableCommands.description: Writes tests that pin down how untested code behaves today, before a change that added behaviour is called done. It does not change the code under test.

availableCommands.name: ux
availableCommands.description: Looks at a changed screen as the person using it: can every part be reached, does each part help you decide or change something, and is each explanation enough to act on. It proposes a lean view and never edits the screen itself.

availableCommands.name: worker
availableCommands.description: Carries out one instruction from the PM or the chief engineer with the tool the instruction names, exactly as written, and reports what the tool did. It is the only seat that changes code, and it never edits a file by hand.
